## How does a language model produce the next token?

An autoregressive language model receives a sequence of tokens and computes a probability distribution over the next token. This apparently simple operation relies on data, numerical representations, attention mechanisms, and a learning objective.

**LLM Lab connects these mechanisms to their mathematical explanations and observable behaviour.** The goal is not to trust an intuition because a diagram looks convincing: it is to understand what a component computes, verify what can be tested, and identify what remains an assumption or limitation.

## A seven-step conceptual route

This is a **reading order**, not the chronology of a complete training run. Evaluation is cross-cutting: it informs data, training, inference, and adaptation decisions. Exercises are grouped separately so they remain accessible from every stage.

The sidebar separates the operations that transform the input, those that compute a prediction, and those that define the learning signal. The suggested order follows the main dependencies without requiring linear reading.

:::: {.learning-route}
::: {.route-step}
**1 · Get oriented**

What does an autoregressive GPT do? How do its components fit into the overall language-model process?

[GPT / Transformer overview](transformer.qmd) · [Historical landmarks](transformer-history.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**2 · Prepare text and data**

How do documents become usable text, then tokens, token IDs, and training examples?

[Text, tokenization, and data](text-data.qmd) · [Training examples](training-examples.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**3 · Represent text**

How do token IDs become tensors and vectors, then context-dependent representations?

[Tensors](tensors.qmd) · [Embedding space](embedding-space.qmd) · [Position](positional-encoding.qmd) · [Contextualized representations](contextualized-representations.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**4 · Compute with the Transformer**

How does attention combine information across positions, and how does causal masking constrain this computation?

[Queries, keys, and values](queries-keys-values.qmd) · [Attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd) · [Causal masking](causal-masking.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**5 · Produce a prediction**

How do final representations become vocabulary scores and then a probability distribution?

[Logits](logits.qmd) · [Probabilities](probabilities.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**6 · Define the learning signal**

How do we measure the gap between predictions and targets, formalize the objective, and obtain gradients for learning?

[Likelihood and entropy](likelihood.qmd) · [Cross-entropy](cross-entropy.qmd) · [Loss and gradients](loss.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-step}
**7 · Evaluate and challenge**

How should we design an evaluation, analyze errors, and distinguish what measurements actually support?

[Experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd)
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note}
**Current scope.** This route organizes the content currently available; it does not claim that a complete GPT has already been implemented. Detailed generation, reproducible pretraining, and adaptation of a pretrained model remain distinct workstreams beyond the conceptual route.
:::

## Verify, do not only visualize

A page may combine intuition, mathematical derivation, code, tests, and experiments. These provide different kinds of evidence:

- a diagram makes a structure readable but does not prove a property;
- a derivation establishes a result under explicit assumptions;
- a test checks the cases it covers but does not by itself prove a general rule;
- an experiment compares configurations under a documented protocol, metrics, and limitations.

Pages distinguish available explanations, code that has actually been tested, and work that remains planned.

## Guided build and intended scope

The guided path aims to build a small decoder-only GPT from randomly initialized parameters: data and tokenizer, training examples, representations, architecture, objective, optimization, validation, and generation. Adapting a pretrained model (classification, instruction tuning, LoRA, quantization) is a separate branch.

The complete path, prerequisites, and evidence criteria are documented in the [curriculum map](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/full-curriculum-plan.md) and [learning path](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md). **A page existing does not mean its implementation, tests, or rendering have been validated**: the sidebar reflects currently available content, not the full intended programme.
